subject: GLM Pmml Bug due to substring match

messages.author: 3d09db67ce330fe9
messages.subject: GLM Pmml Bug due to substring match
parts:
There is a bug in the pmml glm package Below is the detail of the bug

PMML glm package does substring matching for parameters to predictor matching. Hence if we have column names that have similar names PPCell gets all the  predictors - parameter matches. Below is an example of this.
 
data = read.csv("~/test.csv", check.names = FALSE)
df = cbind(data)
fit = glm(out~.,data=df)
library(pmml)
pmml.glm(fit)


test.csv
Test This,Test This 2,out
10,12,0
12,23,1
12,10,0

If you see the "Test This" is a substring of "Test This 2"

  <ParameterList>
   <Parameter name="p0" label="(Intercept)"/>
   <Parameter name="p1" label="`Test This`"/>
   <Parameter name="p2" label="`Test This 2`"/>
  </ParameterList>
  <FactorList/>
  <CovariateList>
   <Predictor name="Test This"/>
   <Predictor name="Test This 2"/>
  </CovariateList>
  <PPMatrix>
   <PPCell value="1" predictorName="Test This" parameterName="p1"/>
   <PPCell value="1" predictorName="Test This" parameterName="p2"/>
   <PPCell value="1" predictorName="Test This 2" parameterName="p2"/>
  </PPMatrix>
  <ParamMatrix>
   <PCell parameterName="p0" df="1" beta="-1.6923076923077"/>
   <PCell parameterName="p1" df="1" beta="0.0769230769230773"/>
   <PCell parameterName="p2" df="1" beta="0.0769230769230769"/>
  </ParamMatrix>
 </GeneralRegressionModel>
</PMML>

For the PPCell value for p2 which corresponds to only "Test This 2" has both the predictors. Which will screw up the scoring as co-effieicents of the second variable get multiplied to the product of "Test This" and "Test This 2" rather than just "Test This 2"

Below is the glm output

Call:  glm(formula = out ~ ., data = df)

Coefficients:
  (Intercept)    `Test This`  `Test This 2` 
     -1.69231        0.07692        0.07692 

Degrees of Freedom: 2 Total (i.e. Null);  0 Residual
Null Deviance:        0.6667
Residual Deviance: 1.245e-30     AIC: -193.4

Looks like there are bunch of greps that might be causing these problems
